Feature/Action: Modal action buttons use consistent labels/order/placement across create and edit modals
Steps: Open New Sub User, New Ticket, and an Edit flow (e.g. edit a Team Contact). Compare button labels, order, and position.
Expected Result: Primary action (Save/Create) and secondary action (Cancel/Close) use the same wording order and position across every modal.

Feature/Action: Save/submit actions show a loading or in-progress state
Steps: Trigger a save with a noticeable network delay (e.g. create Sub User submit a ticket reply) and observe the button/UI during the request.
Expected Result: Button shows a busy/loading state between click and completion; UI does not appear frozen or allow duplicate submits.

Feature/Action: Successful save/create/edit actions show a clear confirmation
Steps: Complete a create/edit/disable/delete action anywhere in scope.
Expected Result: A toast, banner, or equivalent confirmation appears; the affected item updates in the underlying table/view without a manual refresh.

Feature/Action: Modals can be dismissed without side effects
Steps: Open a creation modal, partially fill it, then close via each available method (Cancel, X icon, Escape key, click outside).
Expected Result: Every dismissal method closes the modal without saving partial data or leaving the view in a broken/loading state.

Feature/Action: Multi-select fields show currently selected values without requiring recall
Steps: Open Edit on an item with multiple selections already made (e.g. a Sub User with 2+ Associated Teams).
Expected Result: Current selections are visibly listed/checked in the field itself not just inferable by reopening a dropdown.

Feature/Action: Tables show only the information needed for the primary task
Steps: Open the Tickets table and Sub Users table with default columns.
Expected Result: Default columns cover fields needed to scan/triage at a glance; secondary fields are available via column config or detail view, not cluttering the default view.

Feature/Action: Primary flows are fully operable by keyboard alone
Steps: Using only Tab/Shift+Tab/Enter/Space/Escape (no mouse), open a creation modal, fill required fields, submit; also navigate a data table.
Expected Result: Every interactive element is reachable and operable via keyboard, with a visible focus indicator at each step.

Heuristic: WCAG 2.1 AA - Labels and error identification
Feature/Action: Form fields have visible associated labels and validation errors are shown as text near the field
Steps: Open a creation form and trigger a validation error (leave a required field blank submit).
Expected Result: Each field has a persistent visible label (not placeholder-only); the error is shown as text near the field, not conveyed by color/border alone.

Feature/Action: Status values are distinguishable without relying on color alone
Steps: View a table with status badges/colors (e.g. Sub Users Status column Tickets Status column).
Expected Result: Status is also conveyed via text/icon/shape, not color alone.

Feature/Action: Focus indicator is visible on all interactive elements
Steps: Tab through a form and a table's row actions.
Expected Result: A clearly visible focus outline/highlight appears on the currently focused element at every step.

Heuristic: Match between system and the real world
Feature/Action: Team Profile terminology matches how support/ops staff refer to these concepts
Steps: Open a Team Profile and review field labels and section names.
Expected Result: Labels use terminology consistent with the spec/business language; no internal codenames or ambiguous abbreviations exposed to the user.

Feature/Action: Read-only fields blocked for Partner Administrator clearly indicate why they can't be edited
Steps: As Partner Administrator, attempt to edit Team Name or an Additional Details field on a Team Profile.
Expected Result: The field is clearly shown as read-only/disabled (not silently rejecting a click) and ideally indicates who can edit it.
Notes: Related to PROF-03/PROF-06 functional findings - those confirmed the fields are blocked; this checks whether the UI communicates why.

Feature/Action: Adding a Team Contact without an email is flagged before submit not just on save
Steps: While adding an Additional Team Contact fill Name/Phone and leave Email blank; observe the form before clicking submit.
Expected Result: The missing-email state is flagged inline (disabled submit or inline hint) rather than only surfacing after a failed save attempt.
Notes: Builds on TEAM-05/PROF-07 functional pass - those confirmed the block exists; this checks how early/clearly it is communicated.

Feature/Action: Sub Users table reflects a newly created/edited/disabled user immediately
Steps: Create edit or disable a Sub User and return to the Sub Users table.
Expected Result: The table shows the change immediately without a manual page refresh.

Feature/Action: Associated Teams field is searchable/filterable rather than requiring scrolling a long list
Steps: Open New Sub User and interact with the Associated Teams selector.
Expected Result: If the Teams list is long, the field supports typing to filter; note actual list length observed if short.

Feature/Action: Sub User create and edit forms use the same field order labels and layout
Steps: Open New Sub User then open Edit on an existing Sub User; compare the two forms.
Expected Result: Fields appear in the same order with the same labels and controls in both create and edit contexts.

Feature/Action: Sub Users table can be searched/filtered without leaving the Partner's expanded view
Steps: Expand a Partner with several Sub Users and attempt to locate one by name/email.
Expected Result: A search or filter control is available directly on the Sub Users table not only on a separate global view.

Feature/Action: Auto-filled Description template is presented as editable starting text not locked or ambiguous
Steps: Select a Category/Subcategory with an associated template in New Ticket and inspect the Description field.
Expected Result: It is visually clear the field is pre-filled but still editable (not read-only not indistinguishable from placeholder text).

Feature/Action: A Partner Administrator blocked from Category Management gets a clear reason not a dead link
Steps: As Partner Administrator, attempt to reach Category Management (via nav or URL if discoverable).
Expected Result: User sees a clear not-permitted state (or the option is simply absent from navigation) rather than a broken/blank page.

Feature/Action: Saving an edit on a Team Profile confirms success and shows the updated value without navigating away
Steps: Edit an Additional Team Contact from the Team Profile view and save.
Expected Result: A confirmation appears and the updated value is visible on the same screen immediately.

Feature/Action: Team Profile data matches what's shown elsewhere with consistent field naming
Steps: Compare a field's label and value on the Team Profile view against the same underlying data shown elsewhere (e.g. Sub Users table ticket Team column).
Expected Result: The same underlying field uses the same name and displays the same value across every view it appears in.

Feature/Action: Adding a contact without an Email on the Team Profile view is blocked with the same clarity as elsewhere
Steps: Attempt to add a Team Profile contact with no Email, same check as UX-TEAM-03 from the Profile entry point.
Expected Result: Behavior and messaging match the Team-creation-flow equivalent - no inconsistency between entry points for the same rule.

Feature/Action: Sending a ticket reply shows a sending/pending state and confirms once posted
Steps: Reply to a ticket and observe the UI between clicking Send and the reply appearing in the thread.
Expected Result: A pending/sending indicator appears; the new reply is visible in the thread immediately on success without a manual refresh.

Feature/Action: A ticket reply in progress can be safely abandoned without silently losing a long draft
Steps: Start composing a lengthy reply, then navigate away or close the compose area.
Expected Result: The user is warned before losing unsaved reply content, or the draft is preserved if they return.

Feature/Action: The Close/Escalate/Re-open message-required rule is signaled before the user clicks the action
Steps: Open Close or Escalate on a ticket and observe the button/field state with no message typed yet.
Expected Result: The requirement is visible up front (disabled button with a hint or inline note) rather than only surfacing after a failed click.

Feature/Action: Active filters remain visible on the Tickets table so the user can see what's currently filtered
Steps: Apply a filter (e.g. Status = Open) to the Tickets table.
Expected Result: An active filter is shown as a visible chip/label near the table distinguishing filtered results from the full list at a glance.

Feature/Action: Common ticket actions are reachable without excessive navigation depth
Steps: From the Tickets table open a ticket and locate the primary interactive actions.
Expected Result: Reply/Close/Escalate are reachable within one click/screen from the open ticket view, not buried in a secondary menu.

Feature/Action: Ticket thread visually distinguishes Submitter vs Agent messages beyond the text label alone
Steps: Open a ticket thread with messages from both directions.
Expected Result: Submitter and Agent messages are visually differentiated (alignment, color, avatar) in addition to the text label, aiding fast scanning.
